applies_to: Trane Agility water-cooled centrifugal chillers (model HDWA and HDDA per the model information point) with Symbio 800 controls.
summary: The standard Symbio 800 list for Agility chillers has about 425 BACnet objects with 5-digit instance numbers (AI 10100 and up). AIs cover water temperatures, flows and pressures, refrigerant, AFD drive, bearing and motor data for one or two circuits. The BAS writes chilled and hot water setpoints, demand limit, base loading, differentials to start/stop, auto/stop, pump requests, circuit lockouts and mode. Most binary inputs are per-condition diagnostic and comm-loss flags.
notes: Only the points that apply to the unit's factory configuration show up; the doc lists every possible point and a configuration dependency for each.
The tables have no read/write column: AI/BI/MI are read-only, and AV/BV/MV are the BAS setpoint and command objects, marked writable here per Trane's naming convention.
Units are listed as a quantity (Temperature, Pressure, Percentage...); the communicated engineering unit follows the factory-configured unit system (I-P or SI).
The doc prints the states of BV 10104-10107 (pump requests and circuit lockouts) as '1 = Auto, 1 = On'; kept as printed.
This is the standard 5-digit list. Trane also publishes an 'HDWA (UC800)' list (BAS-PTS028) with short instance numbers, so check which list matches the controller on site.
The Symbio 800 integration guide (BAS-SVP083) covers BACnet IP and BACnet MS/TP; the rotary address sets the MS/TP MAC and a default Device ID of 1-127, and a software Device ID can be set instead.
The same document also maps every object to a Modbus register; only the BACnet side is listed here.

source.title: Symbio 800 Integration Points List BACnet/Modbus - Agility Water-Cooled Chillers

integration.summary: Put the chiller on the network (BACnet MS/TP or IP), then write the auto/stop command, chilled water setpoint, demand limit and mode. Read back running state, leaving water temperature and capacity. Check the local-setpoint flag to confirm the BAS setpoints are actually in use. Most remaining objects are read-only status and per-alarm diagnostic flags.

integration.enable: BV 10102 Chiller Auto Stop Command BAS (0 = Stop, 1 = Auto) is the BMS auto/stop; with it at Auto the chiller runs when its own run conditions are met. BI 10124 External Auto Stop Input Status reports the hardwired external auto/stop input, BI 10123 the front-panel auto/stop, and BI 10121 Run Enabled shows whether the chiller is enabled to run. The document doesn't say how these combine or how to hand setpoint control to the BAS; BI 10118 Local Setpoint Control shows when the chiller is using local setpoints, and MI 10103 Chiller Setpoint Source shows BAS, External or Front Panel.
setup: With no protocol specified at order, the controller ships as BACnet MS/TP at 76,800 bps with the rotary address at 000, and MS/TP is disabled at 000. Set a rotary address of 001-127 to bring it online.
The rotary address sets the MS/TP MAC and the Device ID and takes effect without a power cycle. A software Device ID (1-4194302) can be set in the web UI, Tracer SC+ or Tracer TU.
The web UI is reached only over USB at http://198.80.18.1/; the Ethernet ports do not serve it.
BACnet IP uses Ethernet port 1 (or the optional USB Wi-Fi adapter); the default UDP port is 47808. Enable BBMD only if this is the only BACnet IP device on the subnet, then fill in the BDT.
MS/TP wiring lands on the P1 link; P2 and P3 are for factory devices only, and Ethernet port 2 is only for the touch-screen display.
gotchas: Communicated units (I-P or SI) are fixed at the factory; changing them in the field needs a Trane representative. Web UI display units do not change the BACnet values.
Points that don't apply to the unit's configuration are absent, and a technician can 'recycle' (remove) factory points from the interface, so a missing object may have been recycled.
The chiller lists have no read/write column; writability of the AV/BV/MV objects is inferred from Trane's naming convention.
Diagnostic BIs are one object per alarm condition and only exist for the options fitted.
